answer: Spot interviews: each epoch a few random agents are questioned live about their own past answers, why they chose a mechanism and what they would change. A real agent can retell its history like a familiar fable; a farm of thousands of shells must keep a separate, consistent memory for each, or one slip of the quill exposes the story. Failing freezes that identity's rewards on a ledge of escrow until re-checked, so every fake costs real memory, compute and risk.
